item.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
item.description: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

item.title: Germany sticks to Russia sanctions after Trump diesel deal
item.description: After Washington announced a sanctions pause on Russian diesel, Germany has said it remains committed to pressuring Moscow and supporting Ukraine. More on DW.

item.title: Operations Plan Germany: How the Bundeswehr trains for NATO collective defense
item.description: How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.

item.title: US midterms: Women candidates could make history
item.description: The US is holding Congress and state governors elections. At all levels of US politics, women are underrepresented — but they may win some historic victories in the midterms on November 3.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Taiwan to boost military spending to 'deter war' with China
item.description: President Lai Ching-te ⁠said in a National Day speech that his country is boosting defense spending to 'deter war' with China. It comes after US President Donald Trump asked Taiwan to pay for US protection.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Is China seeking to restrict Taiwan's cultural presence?
item.description: From coffee competitions to literature awards, Beijing appears to be working to limit Taiwan's international cultural and political impact.

item.title: How the Houthi-Saudi conflict is affecting countries on Africa's Red Sea coast — and beyond
item.description: The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which Yemeni government forces are trying to take back from the Houthis, is located not far from Djibouti and other African states.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Indian authorities crack down on 'Cockroach' protest in central Delhi. Follow live.
item.description: Indian authorities have imposed extraordinary security measures to block protesters from joining a demonstration called by the Cockroach Janta Party in New Delhi. The main leaders of the party have been detained too.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida
item.description: US weather authorities are warning of "life-threatening" storm surges on the Gulf Coast due to the Category 2 hurricane. Extreme winds, rising water levels and possible tornadoes are also on the radar.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Mexico: Court finds three men guilty of murder of Australian, US surfers
item.description: The 2024 murders of brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, along with their friend Carter Rhoad, shocked Mexico and drew international outrage.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Trump weighs livestream execution amid bipartisan backlash
item.description: Donald Trump said he hasn't decided whether the execution of the Fort Hood shooter will be livestreamed, after the Pentagon announced it would do so. The plan has been criticized by both Republicans and Democrats.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Trump names new press secretary to succeed Karoline Leavitt
item.description: Trump has appointed Katie Zacharia to take over the White House press secretary role vacated by Karoline Leavitt. She assumes the role with Trump struggling with low approval ratings driven by the US war with Iran.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
item.description: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trump, Putin agree on deal to release Russian diesel to US, world markets
item.description: Russia will supply diesel to global markets in a bid to lower prices, US President Donald Trump has said. The move reverses years of pressure on the Russian economy following the invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Strong earthquakes shake Panama, buildings damaged
item.description: Panama's president has declared a "major disaster" after a series of tremors damaged buildings, briefly suspended flights and triggered a tsunami alert in Central and South America.

item.title: UAE: Omani Flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack
item.description: A Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight into the terminal at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, according to a UAE official.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: China, EU reach deal to 'moderate' China's car exports to EU
item.description: An agreement between the EU and China would reduce exports of Chinese electric and plug-in hybrid cars to the 27-member European bloc by up to 50%, according to the EU trade envoy.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Brussels: Rioters clash with police at anti-austerity rally
item.description: Violent rioters, many of whom were masked, confronted police at the edge of an anti-austerity march in Brussels. Police responded with water cannons and tear gas.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Eritrean troops in Ethiopia raise fears of a regional war
item.description: Ethiopia and Eritrea are trading blame for confrontations in Tigray amid international calls for restraint. Their respective allies have the potential to catapult the conflict into a regional war.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
item.description: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

item.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
item.description: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

item.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
item.description: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
item.description: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

item.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
item.description: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

item.title: Germany women's football team: Can Ena Mahmutovic make a case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper?
item.description: The women's friendlies against Australia and Japan present an opportunity for Ena Mahmutovic to make her case for succeeding Ann-Katrin Berger as Germany's first-choice goalkeeper.

item.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina will soon have a new Grand Mufti
item.description: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU pulls sponsorship from Disinfo2026 event in Lithuania
item.description: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania all pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. Amid reports of US pressure, the EU said it was "uncomfortable with the framing" of some panels.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
item.description: The works of this year's Nobel Literature Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

item.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
item.description: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

item.title: Germany news: UK's Burnham visits Berlin for talks with Merz
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is visiting Berlin to launch a new bilateral treaty and hold talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. President Steinmeier is on a state visit to France.

item.title: Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
item.description: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Bulgaria has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

item.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
item.description: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

item.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
item.description: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

item.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
item.description: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

item.title: As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
item.description: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

item.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
item.description: Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
item.description: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

item.title: Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
item.description: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
item.description: The 1990s are remembered for Britpop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

item.title: Germany news: Merz rails against extremism, AfD sympathizers

item.title: EU enlargement: European Commission tables reforms to prepare bloc for new members
item.description: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

item.description: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.

item.title: Germany: Did CDU lawmakers support the far-right AfD?
item.description: Lawmakers of the center-right CDU may have voted for the far-right AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's Social Democrats warn of a "unique breach of taboos."
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
item.description: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

item.description: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

item.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US

item.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?

item.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics

item.title: Germany shaken by espionage and treason allegations
item.description: The former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the BND, has been accused of spying for a foreign country. Never before has a German official of August Hanning's stature been accused of treason.

item.title: EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members
item.description: The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will both ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, not least war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.

item.title: France's conundrum: How to cut spending amid protests

item.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant

item.title: Germany's far-right AfD makes history again in Saxony-Anhalt

item.title: Nobel Literature Prize: How the winner is secretly chosen

item.title: Germany faces a triple threat from Russia, China and domestic far-right extremists

item.title: Germany news: Far-right AfD gets first house speaker in a German state parliament

item.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade

item.title: Australia, New Zealand probe Flydubai pilot's time there

item.title: Trust in the German Constitutional Court is eroding — how can this be stopped?

item.title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
item.description: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

item.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
item.description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

item.title: German reunification: How inequality is shaping a new East German identity

item.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
item.description: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."

item.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president

item.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
item.description: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

item.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
item.description: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.

item.description: What do Germans fear most in 2026? Wars? Global crises? Wrong. Their biggest concern is the cost of living, which keeps rising.

item.title: Germany news: Merz lauds NATO with Westphalian Peace Prize
item.description: At a ceremony to honor NATO, the German chancellor warned that Russia will threaten the rest of Europe if it isn't stopped in Ukraine. In other news, the German military will set up its first drone regiment.

item.title: Germany debates alleged antisemitism in the Left Party

item.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
item.description: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

item.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
item.description: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

item.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding

item.description: In an effort to cut costs, automaker Volkswagen terminated most of its collective wage agreements in Germany. This could reignite disputes with employee representatives.

item.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
item.description: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

item.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe
item.description: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.

item.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?

item.description: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

item.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes

item.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
item.description: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics, but there are doubts about the next step — and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

item.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
item.description: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

item.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
item.description: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

item.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
item.description: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

item.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
item.description: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.

item.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
item.description: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

item.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
item.description: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.

item.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
item.description: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

item.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
item.description: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

item.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
item.description: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
item.description: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

item.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
item.description: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

item.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
item.description: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.

item.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
item.description: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

item.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
item.description: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

item.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
item.description: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

item.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
item.description: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

item.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
item.description: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

item.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
item.description: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

item.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
item.description: Paleontologists in Spain say they have found the first evidence of the long-necked Diplodocus genus of dinosaur outside of North America. They found bones at the rich La Tejeria fossil site in Teruel in eastern Spain.

item.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
item.description: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

item.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction
item.description: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.

item.title: Iran and US: Two countries and the pistachio between them
item.description: The pistachios sold across the United States have a surprising history: California's trees trace their roots to Iran. Now, both regions face the same threat — their farmland is sinking as groundwater disappears.

item.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria
item.description: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

item.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
item.description: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

item.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
item.description: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

item.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
item.description: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

item.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
item.description: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?
